title: NRS Information Circular No. 2026/14: Guidelines for Estimated Returns by Companies Engaged in Midstream Liquefied Natural Gas Activities

lines.text: NIGERIA REVENUE SERVICE
PLOT 1241, KUR MOHAMMED AVENUE, CENTRAL AREA, ABUJA, NIGERIA
INFORMATION CIRCULAR
No: 2026/14 Publication date: 29TH JUNE, 2026
Subject: GUIDELINES FOR ESTIMATED RETURNS BY COMPANIES
ENGAGED IN MIDSTREAM LIQUEFIED NATURAL GAS
ACTIVITIES
These guidelines are issued for the information and guidance of taxpayers,
tax practitioners, Oil and Gas Midstream Liquefied Natural Gas companies
operating in Nigeria and the public in line with the provisions of the relevant
tax laws.
1.0 Introduction
The Nigeria Tax Administration Act (NTAA) No. 5, 2025, provide for Oil and
Gas Midstream Liquefied Natural Gas companies operating in Nigeria to
submit to the Nigeria Revenue Service (the Service), estimated returns of
its profit or loss for the relevant accounting period. These guidelines are
issued to promote compliance in filing of estimated income tax returns by
a company engaged in midstream operations of liquefied natural gas.
2.0 Filing of estimated income tax returns
A company engaged in midstream operations of liquefied natural gas shall
submit to the Service an estimated tax returns of its profits or losses for
each accounting period for the purpose of income tax. The estimated
income tax returns shall be filed not later than two months after the
commencement of each accounting period.
3.0 Contents of the estimated income tax returns
The estimated tax returns of a company for each accounting period shall
contain a;
a. computation of its estimated revenue, adjusted profit or loss and
estimated assessable profits of that period;
b. computation of its estimated revenue from all sources including
plants condensates, natural gas liquids, liquefied natural gas,
liquefied petroleum gas and any other incidental income;

c. statement of an estimate of amounts to be repaid, refunded, waived
or released to it during that period;
d. schedule of capital allowance showing –
e. the estimated residues at the end of that period in respect of its
assets, all estimated qualifying capital expenditure incurred by it in
that period,
f. the values of its assets, estimated by references to the provisions of
that schedule, to be disposed of in that period,
g. the allowances due to it under that schedule for that period, and
h. a computation of estimated capital allowances for the period;
i. computation of its estimated total profits for that period;
j. computation of its estimated tax payable for that period; and
k. declaration that the estimate was made to the best of the ability of
the person signing the declaration.
4.0 Payment on instalment
The payment of estimated tax payable shall be on twelve equal monthly
instalments. Consequently, the estimated income tax computed is divided
by twelve (12) to arrive at the monthly instalments payable as stated
below:
a. the first instalment is due and payable not later than the third month
of the accounting period.
b. subsequent instalments are due and payable not later than the last
day of each month.
c. final instalment is due and payable on or before the due date of
filing of self-assessment of tax for each accounting period.

ALNG Ltd is engaged in midstream oil and gas liquefied natural gas
activities. The following data was extracted from its estimated income tax
returns for 2026 accounting period ending 31st December 2026.
Estimated Tax payable = US$1,200,000,000
Compute monthly instalments payable during the 2026 accounting period.
Treatment
Estimated Income Tax Payable = US$1,200,000,000
Monthly instalment = US$1,200,000,000/12

5.0 Revised income tax estimates
The Oil and Gas Midstream Liquefied Natural Gas companies will submit a
revised return at any time within the accounting period where there is a
material change in any of the parameters used for the estimate to reflect
the change during the accounting period.

6.0 Review and validation of income tax estimates by the Service
Every estimated income tax return made by a company engaged in
liquefied natural gas operations shall be subject to review and validation by
the Service.
However, the Service may determine the estimates payable by the
company on the Best of Judgement basis where a company does not
provide the estimates as required.
7.0 Sanctions for non-compliance
7.1 Failure to file estimated income tax returns
Any Midstream Oil and Gas company engaged in Liquefied Natural Gas that
fails to file estimated income tax returns on the due date is liable to pay
the following penalty:
a. ₦10million for the first day the failure occurs and ₦2million for each
subsequent day the failure continues;
b. any other sum as may be prescribed by the Minister by an order
published in the Official Gazette; and
c. any other sanction prescribed by any applicable law or regulation.

7.2 Failure to pay estimated income tax (instalments)
Any Midstream Oil and Gas company engaged in Liquefied Natural Gas that
fails to pay any instalment due is liable to pay in addition, the following in
addition to the amount due;
a. A sum equal to 10% of the amount due, and
b. in case of naira liability, interest at the prevailing monetary policy
rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread to be determined
by the Minister,
c. in the case of tax liability in foreign currency, interest at the
prevailing secured overnight financing Rate (“SOFR”) or any
successor rate, plus a spread to be determined by the Minister.
8.0 Transitional compliance requirements
The obligation by a company engaged in midstream operations of liquefied
natural gas to file estimated tax returns of its profits or losses for each
accounting period is effective from 2026 accounting period.
For a company that has 31st December as its accounting year end, the
estimated income tax returns for 2026 accounting period will be filed not
later than 28th February 2026. For such company, payment of monthly
instalment will start from March 2026. The first instalment will be paid not
later than 31st March 2026 while other monthly instalments will be paid on
the last day of each succeeding month.
Due to transition, the company will file self-assessment returns of 2026
Year of Assessment by not later than 30th June 2026 (i.e. within six (6)
months of the end of its 2025 accounting period) and pay the tax due.
Consequently, the company will, in addition to the monthly instalments that
will be paid at the end of each succeeding month beginning from March,
also pay income tax for 2026 Year of Assessment (YOA) not later than the
filing due date of 30th June 2026.
9.0 Amendment or Review of Guidelines
The Service may, at any time, withdraw or replace this Guideline or publish
an amended or updated version.
